transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what has been bringing you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... for a while now, I've been convinced that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. It sounds a little strange to say out loud, but they seem to be sending me little signals. Like through event invitations, the topics they choose for panels, or even who happens to sit near me at networking events. And, you know, even when I try to tell myself it could just be a coincidence... I just can't really let it go. It's been bothering me.
How long have you been feeling this way about people tracking and signaling you—days, weeks, or months?
I'd say it's been about two months. Yeah, for roughly the last two months, I've felt like they've been tracking my meetings and sending me those signals.
Besides feeling that you're being tracked and signaled, have you ever heard voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or seen things that others don't see?

No, I... I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. It's really just the... the tracking and those signals at the networking events that I mentioned. Nothing with my hearing or vision.
Over these past two months, have you noticed any significant changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or empty, or on the other hand, unusually elated, energetic, or irritable?

No, I haven't really noticed any big changes in my mood. I mean, I don't feel sad or hopeless, and I'm definitely not feeling super energetic or anything like that. I'm just... frustrated and a bit stressed out about the whole tracking thing, but my mood itself has been pretty normal, I'd say.
Do you have any medical conditions, recent illnesses, or use any medications, alcohol, or recreational drugs that started around the same time these beliefs began?

No, I don't have any medical conditions. I haven't been sick lately or anything like that. I'm not taking any medications, and... no, I don't use recreational drugs or really drink alcohol. So, there's nothing like that playing a part in this. I'm generally pretty healthy.
Aside from your concerns about being tracked, has this affected your ability to work, maintain relationships, or manage your daily responsibilities?

Well, I'm still working, but... yeah, it has affected things. My practice has actually gotten a bit smaller recently. I find myself missing follow-ups with clients, and... well, I've been avoiding some of the public panels I usually attend. It's just been harder to keep up the exact same level of client contact that I used to manage. So, work has definitely taken a hit.

Have you noticed any changes in the way you think or speak—such as trouble organizing your thoughts, or others telling you your speech seems disjointed—or any loss of motivation, reduced emotional expression, or withdrawal from people outside of this tracking concern?

I haven't noticed my speech being disjointed or anything, and nobody has said my thoughts are disorganized. But... I guess I have lost some motivation. I still get my work done, but just in pieces. I don't really have the same spark for it anymore. Like I said, I'll just leave client follow-ups sitting there. 

And outside of work, I've just been skipping things. I used to go to jazz nights or play pickup basketball, but lately I just skip them, and... I don't really feel much about missing them. When friends ask what's going on, I just give them short answers. Talking just feels like... a lot of effort right now. More than it should.

When did you first start noticing this loss of motivation and pulling back from friends and activities like jazz nights—did that begin around the same time as the tracking concerns two months ago, or had you been feeling that way for longer?

It didn't start two months ago. It's actually been going on for a lot longer. Um, I'd say these changes... like losing motivation and pulling back from things... they've been building since I got recognized by that arts nonprofit. That was a little over two years ago. So, yeah, it's been a while.
I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch that. Could you repeat the question?

Importantly, he also reports over 2 years of negative symptoms—avolition, anhedonia, blunted affect, and social withdrawal—that predate the delusional content and have caused clear functional decline in his professional practice and social life. The combination of prominent positive (delusions) and negative symptoms (avolition, anhedonia, affective flattening) with significant functional impairment exceeding 6 months meets criteria for schizophrenia, paranoid subtype, given the predominance of persecutory delusions. Delusional disorder (F22) is less likely given the presence of negative symptoms and functional deterioration, and schizotypal/prodromal presentations (F21) are excluded by the presence of frank, fixed delusions of this severity and duration.
